title: MixupExplainer: Generalizing Explanations for Graph Neural Networks with Data Augmentation

problem.claim: Graph Neural Network predictions are often not interpretable, motivating methods that explain their prediction behavior through substructures.

gap.claim: Existing post-hoc instance-level explanation methods exhibit a distribution shifting issue that affects explanation quality, particularly on real-life datasets with tight decision boundaries.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces a generalized Graph Information Bottleneck form that includes a label-independent graph variable and is equivalent to the vanilla Graph Information Bottleneck.
The paper proposes MixupExplainer, a graph mixup method driven by the generalized Graph Information Bottleneck.
The proposed graph mixup method is presented with a theoretical guarantee to resolve the distribution shifting issue.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets to validate the effectiveness of their mixup approach over existing approaches.
The authors report a detailed analysis of how their approach alleviates the distribution shifting issue.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph Neural Networks are increasingly used for graph-structured data, but their predictions are often not interpretable.
Post-hoc instance-level explanation methods seek substructures that explain the behavior of trained Graph Neural Networks.
Existing explanation methods are affected by distribution shifting, which can reduce explanation quality, especially for real-life datasets with tight decision boundaries.
The paper introduces a generalized Graph Information Bottleneck form and uses it to propose the graph mixup method MixupExplainer, accompanied by a theoretical guarantee.
The authors report experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets and analyze how the approach alleviates distribution shifting.

source_observation.claim: Explanation methods can suffer from distribution shifting when their explanation process encounters a distribution different from the trained model's relevant data distribution.

interpretation.claim: Explanation quality may depend on whether the explanation mechanism preserves distributional alignment, particularly near tight decision boundaries.

application.claim: When designing post-hoc explanations for graph models, assess and mitigate distribution shifting, including on real-life datasets with tight decision boundaries.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that distribution shifting affects all explanation methods or all datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact generalized Graph Information Bottleneck formulation.
The abstract does not identify the theoretical guarantee's assumptions or formal result.
The abstract does not name the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative experimental results.
The abstract does not describe the graph mixup procedure in implementation detail.
